item.title: Tigers legend Justin Verlander's final career start signals the sad end of an era in baseball
item.description: Detroit Tigers legend Justin Verlander's final start Saturday marks the end of the workhorse era, as no active MLB pitcher may ever reach 300 wins again.
item.content:encoded:
When Justin Verlander steps off the mound for the final time in his illustrious career on Saturday, it won’t just be the final start of his Hall of Fame career. It also signals the end of an era in baseball history: the death of the workhorse starting pitcher.

The leaders on MLB’s all-time pitching lists will likely never change again. Cy Young has the most wins of all time with 511. Verlander, who leads active players by a wide margin, has 266. On the all-time wins list, Verlander is tied for 37th with Bob Feller and Eppa Rixey.

Verlander, who pitched for 21 seasons, won’t be reaching the esteemed 300-win threshold.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

In fact, no pitcher may ever reach 300 wins again. Today, bullpens are more prevalent, starters are pulled from games earlier than ever, and pitchers are getting injured as they chase velocity, shortening their careers. The 300-win pitcher may be a thing of the past.

The active players who trail Verlander on the list? Max Scherzer has 224 wins and is 42 years old, while Gerrit Cole has 162 and is 35. Cole would have to average 20 wins a year for the next seven seasons to reach 300, meaning he would have to pitch at an elite level through his age-42 season to even have a shot.

While it’s hard to bet against Cole, it’s improbable at best. Reaching 300 wins would require remarkable longevity and production.

Just behind Cole is Chris Sale, who is 37 years old with 159 wins. He will not be eclipsing 300 wins either.

In today’s day and age of baseball, 200 wins may be the new 300 wins.

While Verlander and Scherzer won’t reach 300 wins, they are both part of the exclusive 3,000-strikeout club. Only 20 pitchers have ever struck out 3,000 batters in their careers.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Verlander has 3,554 strikeouts, while Scherzer has 3,543, and unlike the 300-win milestone, the 3,000-strikeout club appears more attainable.

Sale currently has 2,779 strikeouts, including 190 this season. With another healthy season or two, the Atlanta Braves left-hander could eclipse 3,000 strikeouts.

Cole has 2,374 strikeouts and has averaged 239 strikeouts over a full season. With three more healthy seasons, he could also enter the club.

After those two, there are no surefire candidates to eclipse 3,000.

Here are the next six pitchers on the active strikeout list:

While some of them have outside chances, reaching 3,000 would require durability and strong production deep into their 30s, which is no sure thing.

At the peak of his powers, Verlander was both durable and productive, and that potent combination made him one of the best pitchers of the century.

Verlander dominated in an era when more was asked of starting pitchers. In addition to his MVP Award, he won three Cy Young Awards and a Triple Crown, was named Rookie of the Year, made 10 All-Star teams, won two ERA titles and is a two-time World Series champion.

Alongside Clayton Kershaw, Scherzer, CC Sabathia and Félix Hernández, Verlander is one of the best pitchers of this generation. Each had multiple seasons with more than 200 innings pitched, a rarity in today's game.

In 2011, when Verlander won the MVP Award, he had a 24-5 record and a 2.40 ERA over 251 innings. From 2007 to 2019, Verlander had only one season in which he finished with fewer than 200 innings pitched: 2015, when he threw 133 1/3 innings.

The death of the workhorse starting pitcher took place over Verlander’s career. In 2006, Verlander’s first full season in the big leagues, 45 pitchers logged 200 or more innings.

In 2026, with some starters having just one more start left in the season, there are only two.

Miami Marlins star Sandy Alcantara has 212 innings, and Philadelphia Phillies ace Cristopher Sánchez has exactly 200. Kansas City Royals right-hander Michael Wacha has 194 1/3 innings, and with a strong final start, he could eclipse 200.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

In 2025, just three pitchers hit the 200 innings mark.

Pitchers may reach similar heights again, but they are unlikely to do it the way Verlander did. The future Hall of Famer's career serves as a harsh reminder of how much the starter pitcher has changed over the years.

So, when Verlander takes the mound for one final time with the Detroit Tigers on Saturday, appreciate his greatness. We won't see anything like it again.

item.title: What is kratom? Risks of popular substance revealed after college students' deaths
item.description: Two University of Mississippi students died with kratom found at both scenes, raising urgent questions about the substance's opioid-like effects.
item.content:encoded:
The deaths of two University of Mississippi students have raised fresh questions about the potential health risks of kratom.

The students died Monday at separate locations on campus. During both investigations, authorities recovered packaged kratom that was purchased from a retail store, according to a Lafayette County Metro Narcotics news release shared by the Oxford Police Department.

Authorities have not confirmed whether the substance played a role in the students’ deaths.

PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY

Kratom is a plant-based substance often marketed as a natural option for pain relief or opioid withdrawal, but experts warn that it can cause dependence, dangerous interactions and other serious health complications.

"Kratom acts as a stimulant at low doses, which could provoke heart arrhythmia," Fox News senior medical analyst, Dr. Marc Siegel told Fox News Digital. "At high doses, it acts more like an opioid, and so can suppress breathing."

Kratom is widely available, Jessica Steinman, chief clinical officer at No Matter What Recovery in Los Angeles, told Fox News Digital.

"We are starting to see it in storefronts, at your local gas stations, smoke shops and health food stores, where it's being sold as an energy booster," she said. "People are starting to buy it over the counter and use it incorrectly, and use mass amounts of it."

DR DREW PINSKY REVEALS RED FLAG IN PRESLEY GERBER ADDICTION TREATMENT BEFORE MODEL'S DEATH

"It's affecting the opioid receptors in people's brains," she went on. "It can cause them to be overly sedated, it can slow down their breathing and general function of their lungs."

Kratom can also become highly addictive, Steinman warned.

Traditional kratom products generally contain lower levels of active compounds, while newer 7-OH products are often concentrated or enhanced to produce stronger, more stimulating effects, she noted.

7-OH products contain 7-hydroxymitragynine, a potent opioid-related compound found in kratom.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

Although kratom laws vary by state and locality, Steinman said regulators are increasingly focused on the concentrated 7-OH products and synthetic kratom-related compounds, rather than traditional botanical kratom containing only trace amounts of 7-OH.

As to why there has been an uptick in kratom use among young people, Steinman said she believes many of them are learning about it from social media or through their friends.

College students may be using the substance for two reasons, she said.

"One reason would be, it is a stimulant," Steinman noted. "They may have pressures to stay awake, to study, get good grades … they may want to be more energized."

People may also be using it due to its opioid-like effects, the expert said.

"It does give someone that sedating high, that kind of numbing out from feeling anything very difficult, not wanting to have to deal with stress or anxiety."

It becomes more dangerous when people combine it with multiple substances, like alcohol, marijuana or benzodiazepines. "That's when it can become lethal," Steinman warned.

People who use kratom and begin breathing slowly or shallowly, or who become excessively drowsy or difficult to awaken, may be experiencing serious sedation that can interfere with breathing, Steinman said. In those cases, prompt medical care is important.

"Another issue that isn't really talked about often is when people might possibly get addicted to kratom," she cautioned.

SORORITY RUSH GETS OZEMPIC MAKEOVER AS SOME COLLEGE WOMEN RESORT TO WEIGHT-LOSS INJECTIONS

Reducing or abruptly stopping kratom after regular use can trigger withdrawal, and in some cases may lead to seizures, according to the expert. Anyone experiencing a seizure should seek emergency medical care.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Steinman also responded to those who might claim that kratom is safe due to the fact that it’s a natural substance.

"Just because something's from the earth doesn't make it healthy — people can get addicted and compulsive with lots of things," she said.

The expert pointed out that there are no addictive components to marijuana, but it becomes addictive – "not necessarily addictive to the brain, but to the feeling that it gives you."

"And that's the same situation with kratom – people get addicted to that feeling. But with kratom, it's actually affecting the opioid receptors in the brain."

Dallas Vasquez, CEO and co-founder of Mitra9 Brands, a Florida-based company that manufactures and sells beverages and products containing kratom (mitragynine) and kava, emphasized the difference between botanical kratom products containing trace levels of 7-OH and products formulated with added, enhanced, highly concentrated or synthesized 7-OH.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The FDA has specifically identified added or enhanced 7-OH products as a particular concern, and the DEA has taken or proposed separate scheduling actions involving elevated 7-OH and related substances," he told Fox News Digital.

Vasquez said Mitra9’s products are made with botanical kratom extract derived from the natural leaf, and not with isolated or synthetic 7-OH.

The products are labeled for adults 21 and older and include precautionary statements, he noted.

The label advises consumers not to exceed the recommended serving, avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, consult a physician before use if taking medications or managing a medical condition, avoid combining the product with alcohol or other substances, be aware that it may be habit-forming, and keep it out of the reach of children.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"We take every report of harm seriously, and we don't dismiss those concerns," Vasquez said, adding that the kratom market is "not uniform."

"Products range from standardized, tested beverages to concentrated and synthetic 7-OH products that federal regulators are now moving to schedule," he said. "We support that action and stronger national standards for testing, labeling, potency limits and age restrictions."

"Consumers deserve to know exactly what is in what they buy, and bad actors should be removed from the market."

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump’s CBP axes Biden-era policy allowing private gifts for illegal immigrants in federal custody
item.description: CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott ended a Biden-era policy letting the agency solicit private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody under Trump's border crackdown.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE – A Biden-era pipeline that allowed federal immigration officials to solicit and accept private gifts for illegal immigrants in custody has been shut down at U.S. Customs and Border Protection, with the agency saying the policy no longer fits the Trump administration's border crackdown.

CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott withdrew the agency from the 2022 Department of Homeland Security directive effective immediately, according to an internal memo obtained exclusively by Fox News.

The directive gave the leaders of CBP and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement authority to solicit, accept and use gifts related to the care of illegal immigrants held in the agencies' custody.

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

"This delegation order is no longer needed or appropriate," Scott wrote. "With the significant decrease in encounters and apprehensions, CBP no longer requires private donations or gifts for distribution to aliens in custody."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

Scott said the policy also "does not align with the Trump administration's strengthened enforcement posture at our borders and related presidential actions issued by the administration."

"For these reasons, I am withdrawing CBP from DHS Delegation 07107, Rev. 1 effective immediately," he wrote.

CBP TOUTS HISTORIC MILESTONE, PUSHES FOR EVEN LARGER WORKFORCE: 'WE AREN’T STOPPING HERE'

CBP confirmed the move to Fox News and said officials recently discovered the directive and moved to rescind the agency's participation. The withdrawal applies to CBP; Scott's memo does not say ICE has been removed from the DHS policy.

The original delegation was signed May 3, 2022, by then-Deputy Homeland Security Secretary John K. Tien.

DHS BUYS TWO CALIFORNIA MIGRANT DETENTION CENTERS FOR $1.5B TO BOOST ICE DEPORTATION CAPACITY

The order also authorized the CBP commissioner and ICE director to solicit specific gifts related to the care of illegal immigrants in custody.

Scott said CBP sought the authority because of the "elevated number of aliens encountered, processed and held" in its facilities at the time. He wrote that the significant decrease in encounters and apprehensions means CBP no longer needs private donations or gifts to distribute to migrants in custody.

"CBP will continue to provide care for aliens in our custody through our normal appropriations," Scott wrote.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham's shirt has a message for the haters, Arch Manning neutralized & Cowboys WAG Haley Cavinder!
item.description: This penultimate Hump Day of September Nightcaps features Sophie Cunningham's 2,000th WNBA point and the Fever's home finale win led by Caitlin Clark.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Penultimate Hump Day of September. It's here. Time is FLYING right now. We're already into Week 3 of the NFL season, and the college football season hits the (almost) quarter mark this Saturday.

We're not taking one second for granted around here. This is the best time of year. I hear Florida's even dipping down into the 60s Saturday morning.

The sixties! We haven't been down there since April. Maybe even March. I've already set my alarm for 6 a.m. just so I can walk outside and catch a whiff of it before the sun rises and melts us all.

Can't wait.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham sends a message to her haters with her pregame shirt before helping the Fever to a win in their home finale.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM THROWS ON A BACKLESS TOP AND OVERTAKES CAITLIN CLARK, TRUMP WAVES THE FLAG & GRUDEN'S BACK!

That's right. The WNBA is still on. Amazing. It's all we could talk about for months, and now it's just sort of buried with football back on. I'll never bury a big Sophie Cunningham night, though. She gets front row seats to this class whenever she wants!

What else? I've got the insufferable outrage mob bullying Arch Manning into becoming a robot, and you will NEVER believe who some in the media think should step in for the injured Jaxson Dart.

Seriously ... this one is an all-timer.

OK, grab you a pot pie for National Great American Pot Pie Day, and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Yes, I've done this before. Heck, I do it every year when this day rolls around. But, for those who forgot — and for those new to class — here's the official Mount Rushmore of Pies:

I'm not just saying that because it's National Great American Pot Pie Day, either. Chicken Pot Pie is so undervalued in 2026. There was a time there in the 80s and 90s when we collectively devoured chicken pot pies. Banquet and Marie Callender's both do mean versions.

Somewhere, though, we've just sort of forgotten about them. They just fell off, as these things tend to do. Feel like we went through the same with toaster strudels.

I still maintain there is nothing better than a nice, hearty chicken pot pie – especially down here in Florida, where it's gonna be a frigid 83 on Saturday!

Welcome back, fall.

OK, let's go ahead and get this class started with Sophie Cunningham telling her haters to "kick rocks" last night before going out there and scoring her 2,000th career point in the WNBA.

Patriot:

Sophie finished with 11 points on 4 of 7 shooting off the bench, and, as you can see, scored her 2,000th career point in the league. Not a bad little night at the arena.

The Fever won, and have just one game left before the playoffs begin. Some girl named Caitlin Clark led all scorers with 27 points last night. Ever heard of her?

OK, let's keep this class moving and check in with Arch Manning, who has been crucified for the past week for laughing at a silly AI video of Steve Sarkisian and Holly Rowe.

He apologized. Sark apologized. The typical lefty sports media freaked out. It was a whole thing.

Manning had his weekly presser yesterday — one week after last week's disaster.

Clearly, the PR folks at Texas got to him:

Amazing. Simply amazing.

Nineteen questions, and only 56 seconds worth of answers. That's almost impossible to do, and Arch pulled it off. Incredible work.

Frankly, it's right out of the Bill Belichick playbook. Give Manning a few more weeks, and he'll be showing up to these pressers wearing a torn hoodie with no sleeves and speaking in such a low grumble, no microphone on earth would be able to pick it up.

Belichick, by the way, still very much has his fastball. Did you see this from last weekend?

He's the best. Even at 74, our guy still has the good stuff.

As for Arch, this was clearly intentional. The media outrage machine wore him down last week, and now they're gonna get absolutely nothing out of him from here on out.

Hope y'all are happy! You've created another boring, vanilla athlete who says boring, vanilla things. Well done!

OK, let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? Guess who NBC's Mike Florio is suggesting John Harbaugh bring in to replace the injured Jaxson Dart?

Joe Flacco? Well, that would make the most sense given his ties to Harbaugh and the fact that he literally just played last season.

But no, not Flacco ...

Colin Kaepernick!!!!

How great is Florio? Some hate him. I love that dude. He's so beyond saving at this point, it's just impressive to watch. He's so brainwashed, and so full of crap, you simply have to respect the game right now. For him to still be virtue-signaling like this after all these years? It's nothing short of admirable.

From Mikey:

It starts with a workout (and quite possibly ends with one). There’s no reason not to give it a whirl. The anthem controversy has subsided. (Harbaugh and the Giants surely would want assurances that Kaepernick wouldn’t dust it off, if he ended up on the sideline before games.)

Seems like just the guy JOHN HARBAUGH wants leading his team!

OK, that's it for today. Good Hump Day, everyone.

item.title: Canadians Nick Taylor and Corey Conners laugh off Lake Ontario renaming ahead of Presidents Cup
item.description: Nick Taylor and Corey Conners laughed off a Lake Ontario naming bet ahead of the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club this week.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Taylor and Corey Conners want to beat the Americans at the Presidents Cup this week. They would prefer to leave the naming of lakes out of it.

Which is unfortunate, because OutKick had a suggestion for adding a little something extra to the competition at Medinah Country Club: The winning team gets to name the lake.

Lake Ontario if the Internationals win. Lake America if Team USA wins.

The two Canadians weren’t sold.

"I think we’ll leave the naming of lakes out of it," Taylor said with a laugh Tuesday.

Conners laughed at the suggestion, too.

"I don’t think anyone would be too excited about that prospect," he said. "I don’t know who’s in charge of lake naming."

Fair enough. Probably not a responsibility either golfer expected to be offered during his pre-tournament media availability.

US PRESIDENTS CUP PLAYERS EXPLAIN HOW CHRISTIAN FAITH BUILDS FRIENDSHIPS AND PUTS GOLF IN PERSPECTIVE

President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Aug. 27 directing that Lake Ontario be renamed Lake America for U.S. federal use, including government maps and documents.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the change.

With Taylor and Conners preparing to face a team of 12 Americans, OutKick asked them about the name change in a series of lighthearted questions.

"I just laughed. That was pretty much it," Taylor said when asked about his initial reaction to the announcement.

Conners said he hadn’t closely followed the news of the name change.

"I honestly haven’t read too much into that. I don’t really have an opinion one way or another," he said. "I feel like being a proud Canadian, I think a lot of Canadians probably still refer to it as Lake Ontario."

So, does any of this provide a little extra motivation to beat the Americans?

"No, that has nothing to do with my motivation," Taylor said. "But our motivation is to come in here and win, so we have plenty of that."

Conners gave essentially the same answer.

"No, I mean certainly not that," he said. "I want to win for my teammates; I want to win for Canada; I want to win for the captains and myself."

Apparently neither needs a lake thrown into the deal with their pride already on the line.

SAM BURNS IS ONE OF AMERICA'S BEST GOLFERS, BUT FAITH, FAMILY AND THE USA MATTER MORE TO HIM THAN GOLF

The Presidents Cup is similar to the Ryder Cup, with 12 American golfers competing against a team of 12 opponents. But while the Ryder Cup pits the United States against Europe, the Presidents Cup’s International team draws players from countries outside the U.S. and Europe. Competition begins Thursday, Sept. 24, at Medinah.

This year’s International team represents seven countries: Canada, Australia, Colombia, Japan, New Zealand, South Africa and South Korea. For Taylor and Conners, that means figuring out how to turn players from five different continents into one team.

"We’re all from different parts of the world, different nationalities, different traditions, different languages," Conners said. "Captain [Geoff] Ogilvy’s done a really great job of getting us together all throughout the year, giving us something to play for."

He pointed to the team’s shield logo as something the players can rally around and said the time they’ve spent together has made a difference.

"We’ve definitely grown close together throughout the last few years," Conners said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Taylor described team dinners, practice rounds and visits to the course as opportunities to build those relationships before the competition begins.

"There’s obviously challenges with everyone growing up in different spots and obviously having different backgrounds," Taylor said. "We made an effort to get to know each other and the camaraderie has been great."

Taylor said a practice round with Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim helped him get to know them better and earned him the nickname "Brother Kim."

"It doesn’t matter who you are, the more time you spend with somebody and you’re all rallying together for one common goal, it’s easy to build relationships and make that stronger," he said.

Any lake-naming negotiations will have to take place elsewhere.

item.title: Paxton’s estranged wife breaks silence on Texas Senate race after 'biblical grounds' divorce
item.description: Angela Paxton urged GOP voters to back Ken Paxton's Texas Senate bid despite their divorce, saying the party seat matters more than personal grievances.
item.content:encoded:
After filing for divorce on "biblical grounds," Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton’s estranged wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton, addressed whether she would support him this November.

In an address to the Texas Federation of Republican Women themed "the elephant in the room," the state senator stressed that "it’s not the people, it’s the seat."

"We have more control over that seat and the future when we control the seat, when it’s still in the family, even if we’re mad at them," she said as the audience chuckled.

Video of the address was posted on Facebook on Friday by the DeWitt County, Texas, GOP and state Republican Executive Committee member Cheryl Thompson-Draper.

FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE

This is the first time Paxton’s estranged wife has publicly addressed the Texas Senate race since filing for divorce. Democrats are targeting the seat as they seek to win control of the Senate. Democratic candidate James Talarico held a 3-point edge over Paxton, 51% to 48%, in the most recent Fox News poll. Fox News has categorized the race as a toss-up.

The state senator filed for divorce from Paxton in July 2025. In her filing, Paxton said that her husband had "committed adultery" and that their marriage had "become insupportable because of discord or conflict of personalities."

In a social media post, she wrote that "after 38 years of marriage, I filed for divorce on biblical grounds."

"I believe marriage is a sacred covenant and I have earnestly pursued reconciliation," she added. "But in light of recent discoveries, I do not believe that it honors God or is loving to myself, my children, or Ken to remain in the marriage."

Despite the divorce, the state senator urged GOP voters to remain loyal to the party in this midterm election.

"If we lose it to the other team, the nuances that we want to fix with maybe a certain candidate are nothing compared to what it’s going to take to get it back," she said.

12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK

She acknowledged that personal frustrations with a candidate may influence some voters but emphasized that "when you vote for the person, the party comes along with them."

"The party comes with the person," she continued. "So, when you vote for that person because you like this one better or whatever, you just need to understand, they are not alone, like a standalone thing, like a menu item, you get the whole thing, and we have more control when it’s our party. We have more ability to influence when that person is attached to our party."

Fox News Digital reached out to the state senator, Paxton and Talarico for comment.

After a bruising primary race in which he toppled longtime Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, Paxton has struggled to find his footing in the general election against Talarico.

Even so, Paxton has projected confidence that voters will reject Talarico as a "fake" moderate, pointing to past comments by Talarico, including saying "God is nonbinary" and saying there are six sexes. Paxton has the support of President Donald Trump and financial backing from the president’s MAGA Inc. political action committee as well as Elon Musk’s America PAC.

item.title: Susan Collins tears into bribery allegations as new claims emerge during critical Senate battle
item.description: Maine Sen. Susan Collins dismissed the FBI bribery probe as a "political hit job," questioning convicted fraudster Martin Kao's credibility.
item.content:encoded:
Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, is addressing claims she was caught up in an FBI bribery investigation, dismissing reporting on the story as the work of Democratic operatives and a known conman.

ProPublica reported that Martin Kao, a former defense contractor CEO and convicted fraudster, told the FBI his company funneled $150,000 through a shell company to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 reelection as part of what he described as a broader pay-to-play operation involving political contributions and government contracts. His cooperation later helped open a new phase of the federal investigation that developed into a broader bribery probe.

Shortly after the story broke, Collins spoke up to dismiss Kao on the basis of his character and called into question the origins of the story. 

"I've got to say, I do not understand how anyone would take the word of a felon who's been convicted twice — twice, two separate cases — of five counts of money laundering, counts of bank fraud, false submissions to the FEC. He is a convicted liar," the senator told The Wall Street Journal’s Kim Strassel.

GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS

In a separate interview with Punchbowl News, Collins blamed Democrats and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for the controversy, calling the report a "political hit job" and questioning its timing.

Collins is embroiled in a heated re-election campaign against Democrat Troy Jackson. Whether Collins keeps her seat could prove crucial to determining which party controls the Senate in 2027. Any hint of controversy for either candidate, naturally, is suited to become a national controversy.

FOX NEWS POLL: MAINE SENATE RACE IS TIGHT, WITH CONCERNS ABOUT BOTH CANDIDATES

Campaign finance records cited by ProPublica show that a shell company established by Kao made a donation to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 re-election campaign. The outlet also obtained emails that it says show Scott Reed, head of the super PAC backing Collins that cycle, was aware of the fact that Kao had used a shell company to mask his illegal donation.

A 2019 email from a naval officer shows that the senator had advocated on behalf of Navatek, the contractor Kao was leading at the time. The email, however, was sent months before Kao routed his illegal donation to Collins’ super PAC. Federal contractors are barred from donating to political campaigns, which is why Kao resorted to a shell company.

FBI spokesman Ben Williamson told ProPublica the agency had investigated claims against Collins years ago "and ultimately found nothing implicating Senator Collins or Senator Collins’ campaign. Any suggestion otherwise is totally false."

The FBI, however, did not respond to ProPublica’s questions about a new investigation it says was launched in 2024 after Kao spent years cooperating with federal agents and detailing his dealings with Collins and other lawmakers.

"The Biden-led Justice Department and FBI totally cleared my office, my campaign and me five years ago of these 7-year-old allegations," Collins said, also not addressing the 2024 investigation directly.

GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS

Kao had a clear incentive to cooperate with the FBI. He was facing years in prison and hoped that providing information would help reduce his sentence, although the judge ultimately gave him no leniency for his cooperation.

"This is a smear job. And as someone who has always prided herself on serving with integrity, it really offends me," Collins said. "And I'm offended for my staff too, both on the campaign and in the personal office."

Collins’ office did not return a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.
